headline: Pretrained RNA language model embeddings paired with graph and state-space architectures
label: Rna Sequence Deep Learning Models
summary: Preprints and publications now pair pretrained RNA and protein language model embeddings with graph, Mamba, and proximal-context architectures.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned representation design for predicting RNA behavior from sequence-derived inputs. CrossLLM-Mamba fuses ESM-2 and RiNALMo embeddings through bidirectional Mamba state-space encoders to predict RNA-protein, RNA-small molecule, and RNA-RNA interactions. OligoGraph applies geometric graph deep learning to siRNA-mRNA duplexes for efficacy prediction, while BioGraphX-RNA and GRASP target RNA subcellular localization using physicochemical interaction graphs and heterogeneous graph neural networks over nucleotide and secondary-structure substructures. What is new is pairing frozen pretrained biological language model embeddings with explicit graph, state-space, or proximal-context architectures. Prism reports that long input sequences can impair gene expression prediction and integrates proximal multimodal epigenomic signals. The same design logic extends to regulatory inference: GReNIMJA, a 2D LSTM, predicts regulatory links for unknown transcription factors at 68.5% accuracy, and Mamba6mA applies a Mamba state-space model to DNA N6-methyladenine site prediction.
